newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU compromises on cross-border payment rules.
newsitem.headline: EU compromises on cross-border payment rules.

text.p: The European Union has agreed in principle in a conciliation procedure legislation to make payment transfers within the EU safer, quicker and cheaper, EU sources said on Monday.
The draft directive on cross-border credit transfers, COM(96)172, will apply to payments of up to 50,000 European currency units, double the amount agreed by EU finance ministers in December 1995.
This follows pressure from the European Parliament which sought to protect individuals as well as small businesses transferring money from one EU country to another.
However, a bank would only be obliged to refund 12,500 Ecus when a transfer is lost under to a compromise struck on Friday by parliament and finance ministers' representatives.

The draft legislation follows the banking industry's apparent inability to agree voluntary rules to improve cross- border transfers, which according to the European Commission and consumer groups are currently lengthy, expensive and unreliable.

A 1993 Commission study showed that beneficiaries often did not get the full amount sent to them because of the banking practice of charging both the sender and the recipient for the service. Banks are also criticised for not accepting responsibility for lost transfers.
The draft rules oblige banks to carry out a payment transfer within five working days and ban double charging.
The rules are expected to be approved finally by finance ministers at their next scheduled meeting on December 2 and the parliament is expected to give its blessing later that month.
But it will be another 30 months before the rules will become law in all EU 15 states, the EU sources said.
